images.title: Angle between clock hands
images.purpose: Show that at 5 o'clock the hands are 5 hours apart, and each hour is 30°, so the angle is 150°.
images.composition: One large round clock face centred with one label line below.
images.exact_structure: One round clock face with exactly 12 evenly spaced tick marks and no numbers. Two hands from the centre: a short hand pointing at the 5 tick and a long hand pointing straight up at the 12 tick, both in teal #0072B2. A amber #E69F00 arc between the hands covers exactly 5 hour gaps on the short side. Exactly 1 clock, 2 hands, 1 arc.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a clock with a number of ticks other than 12
hands not pointing at the 12 and the 5 ticks
images.description: A clock face at 5 o'clock with 12 even ticks and an arc across 5 hour gaps marked 150°, each gap 30°.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the hour gaps in the arc and say 5 times 30.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
